# testdata

Two `.ttc` files produced by **GeoConvert 1.4.5** on 2026-08-03.

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `map_09_4580_9180.ttc` | level 9, tile (139, 291), 2048×2048 DXT1, 12 mips |
| `map_09_4580_9180_mask.ttc` | matching mask, 512×512 L8, 10 mips |

## Provenance

The image content is **synthetic random noise generated by `make_reference.py`**, not aerial
photography and not an IPACS asset. Nothing from the SDK is redistributed here — the repo
`.gitignore` deliberately excludes IPACS tools, and this does not reopen that. What is committed is
the output of running a tool the user already has on input we made ourselves, kept because the
byte-exact rebuild test is worthless without a real file to rebuild.

Regenerate at any time:

```bash
python tools/ttc/make_reference.py --geoconvert "path\to\aerofly_fs_2_geoconvert"
```

## Not committed

The 2048×2048 raw source tile (`map_09_4580_9180_raw.png`, ~9 MB) is skipped to keep the repo small.
`validate_ttc.py` synthesises an equivalent tile when it is absent, which exercises every size and
layout check identically. Pass `--keep-raw` to `make_reference.py` if you want the real one locally
— it is the right input for comparing a new resampler pixel against pixel.
